title: READ ONLY / unverified: the gateway's own Authorization-only calls to originate send no x-tenant-id — single-tenant originate may scope them to DEFAULT_TENANT_ID
description:
## BLUF

**READ ONLY, not driven by anyone.** api-gateway calls originate directly — outside `createProxyRoutes` — at several sites and sends only `Authorization`. With no `x-tenant-id`, originate's KS-458 block (`services/originate/src/index.ts:248-256`) sets `req.tenantId` to `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` in single-tenant mode, so those calls **may** read or write in the default tenant rather than the caller's. Independent of PR #951 (unchanged by it). Raised by the #951 tier-1 gate (round 1, Open item b) and not measured.

## Recommendation

Measure before any fix: drive one site per shape (a read, a write) as a caller in a non-default tenant on a two-tenant local stack and compare which tenant's rows come back. **Unknown that could dissolve this:** whether originate's `authenticate()` sets the tenant from the forwarded JWT on these routes. If confirmed, route gateway→originate calls through one helper that forwards the verified tenant — the same helper #951's F5 residual needs for the vouch.

## Detail

Sites at `develop` `2d864ae92` (grep for the originate URL in `services/api-gateway/src`, headers read at each):

* `routes/proxy.ts:554-556` — `GET /api/signatories`, headers `{ Authorization }`
* `routes/proxy.ts:578-579` — `GET /api/third-party-verifiers`, headers `{ Authorization }`
* `routes/verification.ts:129-138` and `:167-176` — `GET /api/documents/:id`, headers `{ Authorization }` when present
* `routes/batch.ts:146`, `:194` — batch certify / verify via `ORIGINATE_SERVICE_URL`, `authorization` forwarded; `x-tenant-id` 0 mentions in the file
* `routes/platform.ts:249-251` — `POST /api/admin/refresh-tenants`, `Content-Type` + `Authorization`

Not in this ticket (different shape, tracked on PR #951's body as READ ONLY): `routes/verification.ts` `POST /api/documents` and the workflow-approve forward DO send `x-user-id` / `x-tenant-id`, but without the vouch, so #951 would strip them once its secret is provisioned.

**Board searched before filing:** exact `getReqTenantId` → 4 (KS-174, KS-22, KS-26, KS-48 — none about gateway direct calls), `tenantGucContext` → 6 (none), `KS-458` → 1 (itself); control `KS-468` → 1. Fuzzy `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID`, `x-tenant-id`, `signatories`, `third-party-verifiers`, `Authorization-only` → nearest KS-468 (Done — audited the 44 gateway proxy MOUNTS, not these direct calls) and KS-619 (Backlog — `middleware/auth.ts` conditional tenant overwrite).

Related: KS-1041 · KS-468 · KS-619 · PR [https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/951>) · gate report `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-11-ks1041-951-dd0a0c934-tier1/report.md` (Open b).

nodes.title: KS-1084 SIGTENANT TPVTENANT: two gateway reads forward x-tenant-id to originate

nodes.body:
**RULING ON PART B — Kam, live board, 2026-09-22 20:53-20:54.** Card `secuura-ks1084-part-b-api-batch-surface-unauthenticated-dead`, option **a**, verbatim:

> File the ticket for a Claude seat; part B tabled on KS-1084

**Part B is therefore tabled on this ticket and not worked here.**

**The ticket it was to be filed as already exists, so no duplicate was created** (Wednesday's ruling, 2026-09-25): **KS-1243 — "T-3: /api/batch/* is a dead route family - 401 to every caller, 0 upstream hits"**, state Backlog, `archivedAt` null. Searched before concluding that, with `includeArchived: true` and every page literal-matched: `/api/batch` (40 hits), `batch surface 401 unauthenticated` (40 hits), `x-tenant-id` (40 hits); KS-1243 is the top hit on the first two.

**Why Part B is blocked on it:** the api-gateway `/api/batch` surface answers 401 to every caller, so the write site cannot carry `x-tenant-id` until it is reachable at all. KS-1243 is the blocking ticket.

*Delivered by Seat B 24th, 2026-09-25, under Wednesday's confirmation.*

**STAYS IN PROGRESS — #1211 proved the forwarding; the effect this ticket was raised on is still unmeasured.**

#1211 (`0e730fec6`) makes two gateway reads forward `x-tenant-id` to originate — `GET /api/signatories` and `GET /api/third-party-verifiers`, at `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts` — with a test each.

**Remains:**

- **P0 — the cross-tenant effect is not measured.** The *forwarding* is proven. Whether those calls previously read or wrote in `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` rather than the caller's tenant is **not**. The ticket's own recommendation stands: drive one site per shape (a read, a write) as a caller in a non-default tenant on a two-tenant local stack and compare which tenant's rows come back. Until then this ticket's headline claim is unverified in both directions.
- **The remaining sites** listed in the description — `routes/verification.ts:129-138` and `:167-176`, `routes/batch.ts:146` / `:194`, `routes/platform.ts:249-251` — are untouched by #1211.
- **Part B** — see the separate Part-B comment on this ticket.

*Round-20 closing pass, Seat B 24th, 2026-09-25. Kept open by Wednesday's standing ruling.*

## BLUF

**Correction, 2026-09-11: this ticket's body says the workflow-approve forward sends `x-user-id` / `x-tenant-id`. It sends `x-user-id` only.** Nothing else in the body changes. The POST /api/documents forward does send both, as the body says.

## Recommendation

No action needed. The workflow-approve forward's own defect, that it loses the document when originate refuses it, is now KS-1087.

## Detail

- **develop `2d864ae92`, `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:860-864`:** the forward's headers are `Content-Type`, `Content-Length` and `x-user-id` (`:864`, from `pendingDoc.createdBy`). There is no `x-tenant-id` and no `Authorization`. At `02a22f4bb` the `x-user-id` line is `:783`.
- **The POST /api/documents forward** (`http.request` at develop `:1125`) sends `authorization`, `x-user-id`, `x-tenant-id` and `x-tenant-slug`.
- Found while filing KS-1087 from the #951 round-2 gate report. Appended here rather than edited into the body.
